content_text:
You're right: there's no HAT switch, and my premise was wrong. The existing authority is the native state of the capture unit, enviro_dash.service enabled or disabled. Gate the readings lane on that:
- enabled with no fresh readings is a problem;
- disabled is reported as disabled, never as healthy.

Use an existing systemd-state reader. If provider_health has none, report that before adding one.

payload_json.e3: CONFIRMED: one native read, `systemctl show <producer unit from the lane policy> --property=UnitFileState --value`, check=True. Disabled appears as explicit lane detail; a failed query reads observation_unreadable, never healthy. No new flag, store or controller
payload_json.paths: derive rather than configure: at render time the interpreter is sys.executable of the rendering process (the reconciler runs under the project's own venv), and the repo root is the config file's location (write_units already derives root = config_path.parent.parent). No new interpreter field in backup.json, since a configured value would be a second copy of what the process already knows. Implement as a narrow Shared renderer extension that substitutes those two derived values into templates (a placeholder for interpreter and root), adopted by the Enviro backup and provider-health templates in #31. This expansion into Shared is authorized by Bryan's 22:00 'NO hardcoding!' applied to #31. It lands as a small Shared follow-up on main after #8 and goes with the coordinated deploy. Tests: the rendered units carry the rendering interpreter and root; a template still carrying a literal path fails

content_text:
E-3: confirmed. Use one systemctl show UnitFileState read. Disabled appears as explicit detail; a failed query reads unreadable, never healthy.

Paths: derive them, don't configure them. The interpreter is sys.executable of the rendering process, and the root is the config location, which write_units already derives. Don't add an interpreter field; that would be a second copy.

Build it as a narrow Shared renderer extension (interpreter and root placeholders), adopted by the Enviro backup and provider-health templates. It's authorized by Bryan's 22:00 "NO hardcoding!" and lands as a small Shared follow-up with the coordinated deploy. Add tests, including one where a literal path fails. I'll verify.

payload_json.ruling: read LoadState and UnitFileState in the same show call. LoadState=not-found means the producer is not installed, which is how the HAT was taken out of service: report the lane as inactive with explicit detail ('producer not installed'), neither healthy nor a problem. LoadState=loaded with UnitFileState enabled and no fresh readings is a problem. Disabled is inactive with detail. Any other or failed read is observation_unreadable. This follows Bryan's 22:07 direction that adding or disconnecting hardware must not cause persistent failures, and it is interim until pi-config#31 moves the declaration into config. Tests: not-found -> inactive; enabled plus stale -> problem; failed query -> unreadable
